title: Top 6 Loopio Alternatives and Competitors in 2026: AI-Native and Library-Based
summary: Compare 6 Loopio alternatives by category: AI-native tools like Inventive AI and library-based tools like Responsive. Features, pricing, limitations, and ratings.
body_markdown:
*Last reviewed: October 2026. This comparison is based on vendor-published materials, verified G2 reviews, and independent third-party analyses. Pricing and feature details change over time, so confirm current specifics directly with each vendor before purchasing.*


*Magic doesn't work as well as I hoped. It is not the most accurate and requires a lot of manual work."* —[G2 reviewer](https://www.g2.com/products/loopio/reviews/loopio-review-11974149)


That sentiment isn't isolated. While users like Loopio for its easy-to-use interface, collaboration tools, and centralized content library, many also say responses need manual editing, search results aren't always accurate, and keeping the content library up to date requires ongoing effort.


As[AI-powered RFP software](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/why-ai-native-rfp-software-is-replacing-legacy-tools-like-responsive-and-loopio) has improved, many teams are looking for tools that can[generate more accurate responses](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/scale-your-rfp-rfi-response-with-automation-and-ai) , tailor answers, and reduce manual work.


To help you choose, we compared the 6 best Loopio alternatives based on AI capabilities, response quality, pricing, integrations, and verified customer reviews.


**TL;DR**


- **The best Loopio competitors in 2026 split into two categories:** Loopio alternatives split into AI-native tools that generate answers from connected sources and library-based tools that match answers from a curated Q&A library.
- **Best overall:** Inventive AI combines connected knowledge, conflict detection, and narrative proposal support, from $830/month with unlimited users.
- **Best for enterprise workflow:** Responsive and Qvidian, if you can staff library upkeep.
- **Best for project-based pricing:** AutoRFP.ai, from $899/month for 24 projects per year.


## Why should you consider an alternative to Loopio software?


- [AI responses need review](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/blog-posts-ai-in-the-rfp-process-2025) **:** Users report that AI-generated answers can be inaccurate or overly generic, requiring manual edits before submission.
- **Limited document handling:** Complex Excel questionnaires, Word mapping, and formatting often require additional manual work.
- **Search results can be inconsistent:** Finding the most relevant approved content can take extra effort when search returns loosely related answers.
- **Library maintenance takes time:** Keeping the[content library](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/winning-rfp-content-library) accurate and up to date requires ongoing effort from proposal teams.
- **Advanced customization is limited:** Workflow, reporting, and template customization may not meet the needs of every enterprise.

## AI-native vs library-based Loopio competitors: what's the difference?


AI-native RFP software generates each answer from your connected documents and past proposals. Library-based RFP software, the traditional model Loopio uses, retrieves answers from a Q&A library your team curates and updates by hand.


AI-native Library-based


How answers are produced Generated from connected sources Matched from stored Q&A pairs


Upkeep Sources stay current where they already live Library needs regular review and tagging


Main risk Draft quality depends on grounding and citations Answers go stale without an owner


Tools in this list Inventive AI, Arphie, AutoRFP.ai Responsive, Qvidian, Ombud


The shift explains why so many teams look past Loopio, and our breakdown of[why AI-native RFP software is replacing legacy tools like Responsive and Loopio](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/why-ai-native-rfp-software-is-replacing-legacy-tools-like-responsive-and-loopio) covers it in depth. If you stay with a library based tool like Loopio, a[well-run RFP content library](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/winning-rfp-content-library) needs a clear owner.


## AI-native Loopio alternatives


These three tools generate answers from connected knowledge, so they need far less library upkeep than Loopio.


### 1. Inventive AI (best for teams looking for an AI-first alternative to traditional RFP software like Loopio)


[Inventive AI](https://www.inventive.ai/) is an AI-native, agentic RFP platform for RFPs, RFIs, DDQs, security questionnaires, and narrative proposals, with humans approving every response. It suits sales, solutions engineering, and presales teams that want better first drafts and less library work.


#### Why pick Inventive AI over Loopio?


Both platforms help teams automate RFP and questionnaire responses, but they take different approaches to knowledge management and response generation. Loopio centers its workflow around a structured content library, while Inventive AI uses AI agents to retrieve and reason across connected knowledge sources.


Feature Loopio Inventive AI


Core approach Library-first platform built around a centralized Q&A content library. AI-native platform built around AI agents that retrieve and reason across connected knowledge sources.


Response generation Finds and reuses relevant answers from the content library, with users reviewing and adapting responses where needed. Generates contextual responses by analyzing the question, intent, and relevant source content.


Content management Requires teams to maintain and update the centralized content library through review and approval workflows. Reduces reliance on manual library maintenance by pulling information directly from connected sources.


Knowledge sources Organizes reusable content around a centralized library with integrations to other systems. Connects to multiple internal knowledge sources, including documents, drives, wikis, and other repositories.


AI accuracy AI-assisted response generation supported by existing content controls and human review. Near-zero hallucinations, with responses grounded in connected company knowledge and designed to avoid unsupported answers.


Workflow & collaboration Project management, task assignment, review workflows, and content governance. AI-assisted collaboration focused on faster drafting, review, and response completion.


Implementation Teams typically need to structure and populate a content library as part of implementation. Connector-led ingestion lets teams leverage existing knowledge sources without first building a comprehensive Q&A library.


User access Seat-based plans can limit the number of users included depending on the package. Unlimited users, allowing sales, proposal, security, and subject-matter experts to collaborate without individual seat costs.


Pricing approach Custom/seat-based pricing depending on plan and requirements. Starts at $830/month, with unlimited users and usage based on RFP volume.


Best suited for Teams that prioritize structured content governance, centralized libraries, and controlled workflows. Teams that prioritize AI-led response generation, distributed knowledge retrieval, and less manual content maintenance.


The difference matters most if your team is dealing with information spread across multiple systems or spends significant time maintaining reusable answers.


- **Near-zero hallucinations:** Inventive AI is designed to ground responses in your organization's source material, helping reduce unsupported or inaccurate claims in customer-facing responses.
- **Less reliance on a centralized library:** Inventive can retrieve information from connected sources, so teams don't have to consolidate every useful piece of knowledge into a single Q&A database before they can put it to work.
- **Less manual upkeep:** When information changes frequently, working from connected sources can reduce the burden of continually reviewing and updating duplicate answers in a content library.
- **Broader team access:** Unlimited users make it easier to bring sales engineers, security teams, product experts, and other SMEs into the response process without adding individual seat costs.
- **Contextual response generation:** Inventive is designed to use the context of the question and relevant source material to generate a response, rather than relying solely on finding a previously written answer.

### 2. Arphie


Arphie is an AI-native platform for RFPs, security questionnaires, and DDQs that connects to live sources and shows confidence scores and source links for each draft.


#### Arphie best features


Arphie's best features are live knowledge connections, explainable AI drafts, and enterprise security controls.


- **Live sources:** Connects to Google Drive, SharePoint, Confluence, Notion, Seismic, and Highspot.
- **Explainable drafts:** Confidence scores, source links, and reasoning for each answer.
- **Duplicate merging:** Identifies and merges duplicate Q&A entries.
- **Security:** SOC 2 Type II, SSO, encryption at rest and in transit, and role-based access.


#### Arphie limitations


- Import, export, and formatting need work per user reviews
- Reporting is less mature than established platforms
- No built-in competitive intelligence, and narrative proposal support is less comprehensive


#### Arphie pricing


- Arphie does not publish pricing publicly.

### 3. AutoRFP.ai


AutoRFP.ai is an AI-native response platform with a hybrid knowledge approach, built for sales and bid teams, with unlimited users on every plan.


#### AutoRFP.ai best features


AutoRFP.ai's best features are cited AI drafts with confidence scores, a Project Agent for extra tasks, and unlimited users on every plan.


- **Cited drafts:** AI responses include source citations and confidence scores.
- **Project Agent:** Handles executive summaries, response edits, and web research.
- **Formats and languages:** Supports Word, Excel, and PDF, and translates into 44+ languages.
- **Unlimited users:** Integrates with SharePoint, Confluence, Salesforce, Slack, Teams, and Google Drive.


#### AutoRFP.ai limitations


- Pricing is based on annual project volume, which may not suit teams with unpredictable workloads.
- The user interface can feel less intuitive, and some workflows may require additional effort to navigate.
- Does not include built-in AI-powered conflict detection for identifying outdated, duplicate, or conflicting content.
- AI content governance capabilities for maintaining knowledge quality across sources are more limited compared to AI-native platforms.


#### AutoRFP.ai pricing


- **Scale:** $899/month (billed annually) for **24 projects/year** , with unlimited users, AI, integrations, and support.
- **Accelerate:** $1,299/month (billed annually) for **50 projects/year** . Enterprise pricing is available for higher project volumes.

### Library-based Loopio alternatives


These three tools keep the traditional Q&A library model, like Loopio, and add enterprise workflow, permissions, or publishing controls. Expect ongoing library upkeep with each.


### 4. Responsive (formerly RFPIO)


Responsive is an enterprise response management platform for RFPs, security questionnaires, DDQs, and proposals. It is the closest like-for-like replacement for Loopio.


#### Responsive best features


Responsive's best features are AI-drafted answers with source citations, automatic security questionnaire answers, and wide integration coverage.


- **AI Assistant and agents:** First drafts come with source citations.
- **Security questionnaires:** Answers security questionnaires and vendor risk assessments automatically.
- **Integrations:** About 30 native integrations and 75+ APIs.
- **Languages:** 23+ languages with linked content versions.
- **Project-based collaboration:** Occasional contributors join without needing a license each.


#### Responsive limitations


- AI is built on a traditional Q&A library rather than a live knowledge model.
- Does not identify conflicting or inconsistent content across the knowledge base.
- Lacks built-in competitive intelligence or win-theme recommendations.
- Responses primarily rely on shared content libraries instead of tailoring answers to each buyer or opportunity.
- Users report that AI may generate content outside approved sources, requiring additional review in regulated industries.


#### Responsive pricing


- Starts at **$5,000/year for 5 users (Lite plan)** , with higher tiers for growing and enterprise teams.
- Mid and enterprise plans are **custom-priced** based on users, features, and deployment needs.
- Overall pricing is **quote-based with per-user licensing and add-ons** , so costs vary by scale.

### 5. Qvidian


Qvidian, part of Upland Software, is an enterprise proposal platform with workflows, approvals, and deep Microsoft Office integration. It fits large organizations with dedicated proposal admins.


#### Qvidian best features


Qvidian's best features are governed workflows, a versioned content library, and native Microsoft Office integration.


- **AI Assist:** Generates, revises, and personalizes proposal content inside existing workflows.
- **Content library:** Version control and content expiration for reusable approved responses.
- **Workflows:** Task assignments, approvals, and document parsing.
- **Microsoft integration:** Native Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Teams support.


#### Qvidian limitations


- Search results can be inconsistent, making it harder to find the most relevant content quickly.
- Premium pricing may not suit teams that only use a small subset of the platform's features.
- AI capabilities may require additional review and refinement for complex or highly specific responses.
- Does not offer built-in AI-powered conflict detection for identifying outdated, duplicate, or conflicting content.


#### Qvidian pricing


- Qvidian offers quote-based pricing tailored to your organization's size and requirements and does not list its pricing publicly.
- But, most organizations pay between $15,000 - $25,000/year for the base license (based on third party review data).

### 6. Ombud


Ombud is a response platform for RFPs, security questionnaires, proposals, and SOWs, focused on collaboration, content governance, and publishing to branded templates.


#### Ombud best features


Ombud's best features are repository-based answer suggestions, built-in collaboration, and flexible publishing.


- **OmMatch:** Suggests answers from a centralized, continuously updated content repository.
- **Collaboration:** Task assignments, version history, content approvals, and team workspaces.
- **Multiple response types:** RFPs, security questionnaires, proposals, and SOWs.
- **Publishing:** Exports to Word, Excel, PDF, branded templates, and web portals.


#### Ombud limitations


- Assignments and uploads can feel less intuitive
- Limited native multilingual support
- Pricing is not public


#### Ombud pricing


- Ombud does not publish pricing publicly.
- They offer quote-based pricing based on team size, deployment, and required features.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### How much does Loopio cost?


Loopio does not publish prices and quotes custom annual contracts. Our Loopio pricing guide breaks down what drives the quote.


### Loopio vs Responsive: which is better?


Neither wins on every point, because both draw answers from a Q&A library. Responsive adds deeper project management and permissions for large enterprises and starts at $5,000/year for 5 users.


### Which Loopio alternative is best for security questionnaires?


Inventive AI is the best alternative to Loopio, it answers security questionnaires from connected sources. Inventive AI's security questionnaire software also covers RFPs and narrative proposals in the same platform.


### Can I migrate my Loopio content to another tool?


Yes. Most platforms like Inventive AI import existing libraries, templates, and past proposals, but migration support varies, so confirm the process with each vendor.
